summary.oneLiner: Cyber Media (India) Limited is a B2B media house serving the technology and business sectors, monetising ICT-focused print magazines, online platforms, subscriptions, events and custom marketing solutions.
summary.business: CyberMedia publishes ICT industry magazines and runs online platforms, social channels and video content offering news, analysis and insights for the technology and business sectors. Alongside publishing it sells subscription research and in-depth reports, hosts bespoke and industry events, and provides business solutions to ICT vendors including conferences, lead generation and influencer marketing. Its revenue is described as a mixed model of advertising (print and digital), subscriptions, event sponsorships and custom content solutions, and its reported operating segments are named Media …

currentContext.strengths: Authoritative content, deep industry connections and a strong reputation in the B2B media landscape, stated to attract a loyal audience and respected advertisers|Established ICT publishing brands - Dataquest, PCQuest and Voice&Data - described as leading ICT industry magazines|Diversified revenue streams across advertising, subscriptions, event sponsorships and custom content solutions, stated to stabilise income and reduce dependency on any single revenue source|No customer concentration: the standalone accounts state that no customer accounts for 10% or more of total revenue|Proprietary internally developed systems - the Arya ERP/MIS platform and the Mudra subscription management system - plus a migrated new-generation CMS credited with improving website traffic|Owns building space that is being monetised: space has been leased to Canara Bank and Indian Bank for better asset utilisation|Subscription services growth described as robust despite a slowdown in digital advertising, on the strength of high-value content
currentContext.strategies: Diversification: expanding digital content offerings, including a bigger presence on social media and video monetization|Innovation: using technology to enhance content delivery and engagement; websites have been migrated to a new CMS, which management links to improved overall website traffic|Market Penetration: targeting untapped and emerging markets to expand the client base|Digital-first approach delivering integrated media platforms/brands, a multi-format content strategy, large media property creation and automated, disruptive distribution|Transformation agenda that reimagines all functions in an AI world, with internally developed AI-driven systems to streamline processes and drive efficiency - stated to remain part of the agenda for the foreseeable future|Build out video as the avenue for expanding the brands' circle of influence and outreach, including a video studio being set up for digital assets|Automation of internal processes through the internally built Arya ERP/MIS platform and the new Mudra subscription management system, to improve operational efficiency and customer experience|Maintain a tight watch on costs and continue cost optimisation across businesses and functions, with continued focus on improving profitability|Monetise owned property: space in the Company's building has been leased to Canara Bank and Indian Bank for better asset utilisation|Simplify the group structure by merging subsidiary Cyber Media Research & Services Limited into Cyber Media (India) Limited (fresh scheme approved January 24, 2026; application pending with stock exchanges/SEBI)|A stated 'four-pronged strategy to strengthen our relevance with clients and drive accelerated value creation' is referenced but the four prongs are never enumerated in the routed text|No dividend is recommended for the year under review - the Directors' Report states this is 'in the absence of profits' - and no amount has been transferred to reserves. The year's capital-allocation action was equity raising and balance-sheet repair rather than distribution: the Rights Issue Committee approved a Letter of Offer on July 21, 2025 offering 62,66,897 shares at INR 15.80 per share (including a INR 5.80 premium), aggregating INR 9.90 crore, payable 50% on application and 50% on the First & Final Call; part of the application money took the form of a loan conversion; partly paid shares were allotted on September 02, 2025, the First & Final Call was made in February 2026 and 49,53,415 shares were treated as fully paid on February 20, 2026; after a Final Reminder cum Forfeiture Notice dated March 05, 2026, a further 37,735 shares were made fully paid on April 11, 2026 and the remaining 1,71,329 partly paid shares were forfeited. Structurally, the Board is pursuing group simplification by merging subsidiary Cyber Media Research & Services Limited into the parent (fresh Draft Scheme approved January 24, 2026; pending stock exchange/SEBI approval). Corporate Social Responsibility provisions are stated not to apply because the Company's net worth, turnover and net profit are below the Section 135 thresholds. Management states it maintains a tight watch on costs, is pursuing cost optimisation across businesses and functions, and has leased space in its own building to Canara Bank and Indian Bank for better asset utilisation. No buyback, debt-reduction target, credit rating or formal dividend policy is disclosed.
currentContext.expansion: The section routed to this bundle contains NO capex or expansion content at all (see extraction_notes). Back-filled from sibling bundles with provenance: per the MD&A 'Our Technology Stack and Automation Drive' section (routed to the profile / strategy_outlook / risks_esg bundles), the only physical build-out CyberMedia describes is a video studio it is investing in setting up for its digital assets, to bring focus on video content generation - no cost, size, location or completion date is stated. The other 'expansion' is asset-light and technology-led: websites have been migrated to a new-generation CMS for improved content discovery, SEO, distribution and social amplification, which management links to improved website traffic; an internally developed ERP/MIS platform 'Arya' and a new internally developed subscription management system 'Mudra' have been built; and advanced performance-management and employee-onboarding systems have been added. Footprint change is by monetisation rather than addition - the MD&A 'Business Outlook' section states the Company has leased space in its own building to Canara Bank and Indian Bank for better asset utilisation. The only structural corporate expansion action is the proposed merger of subsidiary Cyber Media Research & Services Limited into Cyber Media (India) Limited (fresh Draft Scheme approved by the Board on January 24, 2026; application pending with the stock exchanges/SEBI), per the Directors' Report routed to the profile and strategy_outlook bundles. The Directors' Report 'Risk Management' paragraph in THIS bundle lists 'expansion of facilities' only as a generic category of common business risk; it describes no actual facility project. No rupee capex quantum, capital commitment, project pipeline, commissioning schedule or new-location plan is disclosed anywhere in any routed section.

a structural shift of advertiser preference toward targeted, data-driven digital formats|Print is comparatively resilient in India: total newspaper revenue is forecast to grow at a 2.7% CAGR from INR 26,378 crore in 2021 to INR 29,945 crore in 2026, and India is stated to be the only country in the world growing daily print newspaper and magazine copy sales by volume, at a 1.3% CAGR to an average 139 million daily copies in 2026|OTT video is set to expand at a 14.1% CAGR to INR 21,032 crore in 2026, with subscription's share of that revenue rising from 90.5% in 2021 to an expected 95% by 2026, accelerating migration of audiences and advertiser budgets to digital|Company-level demand narrative: management describes FY2024-25 as a disappointing year in which it made a conscious effort to turn around the decline, and FY2025-26 as a year in which growth was regained, with an improving business scenario|Subscription services growth described as robust despite a slowdown in digital advertising, attributed to high-value content|Social media growth across LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube, and new strategic partnerships with major tech firms for content co-creation and event hosting, cited as the year's growth drivers|Emergence of digital connectivity presents newer and more intense ways of engaging consumers, with innovation expected in content formats, means of dissemination and business models|AI is flagged as both opportunity and threat: management is watching how the industry changes on AI and how major companies like Google and Meta adapt, and believes CyberMedia's strong presence in the B2B community is the offsetting opportunity|As the community grows, management expects more digitally led monetization opportunities in the coming period for flagship brands Dataquest, PCQuest and Voice&Data through video and social media advertising

risks.risk: Advertising-spend dependence - market dynamics and the reduction or shift in clients' marketing spend
risks.note: Listed first in the MD&A 'Risks and challenges'. CyberMedia's mixed revenue model leans on advertising (print and digital), event sponsorships and custom solutions bought out of ICT vendors' marketing budgets, so a cut or reallocation of client marketing spend transmits directly to revenue. Management separately notes a slowdown in digital advertising during the year, which subscription growth had to offset.

risks.risk: Inadequate client acquisition and revenue growth
risks.note: Explicitly flagged in the MD&A 'Risks and challenges' list. Growth depends on penetrating untapped and emerging markets to expand the client base; failure to add clients caps the top line. Management frames FY2024-25 as a disappointing year it had to consciously turn around, so the risk has recently materialised.

risks.risk: Structural disruption of media by AI and by the platform giants
risks.note: Management states it is keeping a close eye on changes to the entire industry based on AI and on how major companies like Google and Meta adapt, and calls this both an opportunity and a threat. With dynamic technological innovations taking place, the media sector is stated to face considerable uncertainty. The offsetting claim is CyberMedia's presence in the B2B community.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition in digital from imitators and niche players
risks.note: The Company anticipates increased competition in the Digital domain from other businesses trying to emulate it and from several niche enterprises in digital media, social media and other online services. It also lists 'competition from emerging digital platforms and other social media apps' among risks and uncertainties. Its defence is stated to be expertise and brand position as a single-stop shop.

risks.risk: Cybercrime, data breach and data-protection compliance
risks.note: The MD&A names the inherent risk of cybercrimes and data breach that may impact reputation. An Information Officer is entrusted with maintaining the requisite security posture, and the Company states it is proactively working towards DPDP Act compliance and the consent-management systems needed to secure owned and client data - i.e. the compliance work is in progress, not complete.

risks.risk: Execution risk on new initiatives, community building and post-revamp traffic
risks.note: Three of the five items in the MD&A 'Risks and challenges' list are execution risks the Company set for itself: 'Adequate community development', 'New initiatives taking time and not kicking off', and 'Traffic growth post tech revamp'. This matters because the stated strategy - digital-first, video, subscriptions, the Mudra and Arya platforms and the new CMS - is entirely dependent on those initiatives converting.

risks.risk: Content quality and editorial credibility in an environment of fake and low-quality content
risks.note: Management identifies the increasing spread of fake and bad quality content as a major concern for social media. Since CyberMedia's stated USP is authoritative content and reputation, an editorial-credibility failure attacks the asset itself. Mitigation cited is continuous engagement with the editorial team and upgradation of editorial processes to ensure factual accuracy of content published.

'Exposure to litigations' is listed among the risks and uncertainties that can affect the business; no specific or material case is disclosed. The Company states it monitors the status of statutory compliances across all locations and functions to minimise non-compliance exposure. The Directors' Report separately records that neither the statutory auditor's nor the secretarial auditor's report contains any qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer, and that no fraud was reported under Section 143(12).

risks.risk: Talent retention and attrition in a 65-person organisation
risks.note: The Directors' Report lists retention of talent among the Company's common risks, and discloses an overall attrition rate of 18.65 percent as at March 31, 2026 against a total headcount of 65 employees as on that date. At that scale, attrition at that rate is a structural key-person and capability risk for an editorial and content business.

risks.risk: Technology obsolescence and other common business risks named by the Board
risks.note: The Directors' Report 'Risk Management' section enumerates the common risks as regulations, competition, business risk, technology obsolescence, investments, retention of talent and expansion of facilities, with business risk further including financial, political and legal risk. The Company has a Risk Management Policy reviewed by the Audit Committee, and a Risk Management Committee reviews operational, financial, strategic and regulatory risk areas.

one-line thesis: CyberMedia has resolved legacy US business and litigation issues, enabling a sharp rebound in Q1FY26 revenue (+25.5% YoY) and EBITDA (+485% YoY); the company is now strategically pivoting to AI-powered data products and multi-form media monetization, with a Rs. 10 crore rights issue to fuel growth in semiconductor, EV, and subscription analytics.
financial scorecard: revenue: 26.08 Cr (+25.5% YoY); EBITDA: 1.58 Cr (+485% YoY); PAT (rptd): 1.3 Cr (vs negative prior); PAT (normalized): 1.3 Cr (no one-offs); order book: not disclosed; net debt: reduced via rights issue (legacy debt from promoters being converted to equity)
guidance: revenue growth: confident of robust FY26; margin: improving due to digital efficiency; order inflow: expanding in Middle East for data analytics; capex/commissioning: minimal; focus on product development and digital infrastructure
segment / subsidiary detail: B2B Media: 43-year-old brands (DataQuest, PCQuest, CIOL) with 11M+ website users, 3L subscribers; Digital Marketing: Google-certified partner with CM Galaxy & AuxoAds AI platforms; Data Analytics: first-party surveys, custom dashboards, semiconductor/autonomous vehicle reports; Startup Investment: 20+ active startups, 5-10 new/year
growth verticals / optionality: Monetizing 43-year archival content via university subscriptions (MIT already onboard); OTT licensing talks underway; potential launch of new magazines in EVs, semiconductors, drones; CMRSL merger under consideration
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved from 1.3% (Q1FY25) to 6.06% (Q1FY26); cost optimization from digital transition and closure of US ops; no material cost inflation cited
capex / expansion: minimal; focus on digital infrastructure and AI tools (CM Galaxy, AuxoAds); no large physical capex planned
capital allocation: Rs. 10 Cr rights issue: Rs. 3.31 Cr working capital, Rs. 2.5 Cr growth, Rs. 40L expenses; promoter group (61.79% stake) contributing ~75% of funds; legacy debt to equity conversion; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: Dependence on Google/Meta partnerships; slow monetization of archival content; regulatory risk in SME-listed subsidiary; execution risk in new verticals (semiconductors, EVs); potential dilution from rights issue
management quality / tone: Highly confident, transformational, and forward-looking; management emphasizes legacy resolved, digital-first pivot, and AI-driven growth; tone is upbeat and decisive, with clear intent to rebuild market value
non-obvious takeaways: Archival content from 43 years of tech journalism (including coverage of Infosys, Premji, etc.) is being repackaged as premium B2B research assets — a moat few analysts recognize; MIT subscription is a stealth validation of IP value
